executiveSummary: Election-focused synthetic media threats dominate this cycle. U.S. federal advisories warn that threat actors are using deepfake audio/video alongside AI-enhanced phishing and smishing against campaigns and election officials, elevating risks of credential theft, impersonation, and fraud. Security Advisory Concurrently, criminals are impersonating candidates, campaigns, and government entities with AI-generated voices, images, and text to siphon donations and personal data from voters and donors. Security Advisory Foreign-linked influence networks are active. Investigations report China-linked personas posing as U.S. voters on social media and likely Russia-linked disinformation videos targeting Senate races, intensifying pre-election manipulation pressure. View Article View Article Outside elections, UK authorities report £24.3 million stolen across 1,300+ cases via AI-enabled "investment endorsement" schemes leveraging deepfake images and videos, disproportionately harming older adults. View Article Law-enforcement impersonation via voice cloning is also proliferating, with Florida residents targeted by calls faking a sheriff's captain to coerce payments. Source View Article Defensively, provenance and platform countermeasures continue to advance, including operational C2PA/SynthID checks and newsroom-grade authenticity workflows; the EU's Article 50 transparency obligations for deepfakes are also in force. Supporting Report View Article Supporting Report Net assessment: With simultaneous election-targeted deepfakes, foreign-linked influence operations, large-scale financial scams using synthetic media, and credible law-enforcement impersonation via voice cloning, the near-term threat environment appears to be worsening.
